observations: No volume unit is given anywhere in the Water or HKEx sheets; every value column is headed "Consumption" even for withdrawal and discharge tables (mislabel). ML assumed (MMG reports per MCA Water Accounting Framework). Treat unit as unverified.

Internal inconsistency on 2022 consumption: Water sheet (GRI 303-5) gives Kinsevere 4,216.96 and total 22,587.66, while the HKEx sheet gives Kinsevere 4,992 and total 23,363; Kinsevere intensity 1.80 vs 2.13 and total 0.46 vs 0.48. Other sites agree (Dugald River 2,203.70 vs 2,204 is rounding).

Consumption is not simply withdrawal minus discharge (e.g. Dugald River 2,665.4 - 513.8 = 2,151.6 vs 2,203.7 reported; Kinsevere 19,219.6 - 14,972.0 = 4,247.6 vs 4,216.96/4,992), implying storage change/entrainment terms not disclosed.

2022 total withdrawal 54,361; 85% (46,360) is from sites in WRI "Medium - High Stress (2-3)" areas (Dugald River, Kinsevere, Las Bambas); only Rosebery is Low stress (0-1). Sites flagged "medium" in sites[] reflect this Medium-High band.

Las Bambas is the largest user (24,475 withdrawal, 15,224 consumption) but mostly "Other water" (21,426) with only 3,049 freshwater; Kinsevere is 85% freshwater (16,270.8 of 19,219.6) and 78% groundwater.
Consumption 2021 -> 2022 (HKEx): total 23,980 -> 23,363; Dugald River 2,557 -> 2,204; Kinsevere 4,544 -> 4,992; Las Bambas 15,958 -> 15,224; Rosebery 921 -> 943.

Methodology: all operations commenced a gap analysis against the ICMM Water Reporting Good Practice Guide (Aug 2021) with an implementation plan due mid-2022 and compliance reporting from 2023 (Water!B54). 2022 assurance (CECEP) covered Las Bambas and included "Responsible water consumption". Site-specific water targets exist but no values given.
No water incidents, fines, reuse/recycling volumes or production data disclosed in this workbook. Data on 100% equity basis, calendar year.
